tip:
HttpClientRequestMapper<T> was not found. This mapper converts HTTP client method request body type T to an outgoing HTTP request body.
    If the body should be JSON, annotate the client method body parameter with @Json and make sure JsonWriter<T> exists.
    If this is not JSON, provide a custom HttpClientRequestMapper<T> component or use @Mapping(...).

If this HTTP client was generated from an OpenAPI specification, ensure that the request body declares Content-Type: application/json when JSON mapping is expected.
    Example: requestBody -> content -> application/json.
    If the content section is missing or has another media type, the generator will not apply @Json for the request mapper.

HttpClientParameterWriter<T> was not found. This writer converts HTTP client path, query, header, or cookie parameter type T to a string value.
    Kora provides writers for common scalar types and can use JsonWriter<T> for @Json parameters.
    If T is a custom type, provide a custom HttpClientParameterWriter<T> component or use @Mapping(...). Maybe the writer tag was forgotten or mixed up if this dependency uses @Tag(...).

HttpClientResponseMapper<T> was not found. This mapper converts an HTTP client response body to method result type T.
    If the response should be JSON, annotate the client method return type with @Json and make sure JsonReader<T> exists.
    If this is not JSON, provide a custom HttpClientResponseMapper<T> component or use @Mapping(...).

If this HTTP client was generated from an OpenAPI specification, ensure that the response declares Content-Type: application/json when JSON mapping is expected.
    Example: responses -> '200' -> content -> application/json.
    If the content section is missing or has another media type, the generator will not apply @Json for the response mapper.
